questions.q: In medicine, targeted therapy acts on the specific genes that drive a disease. What does the editorial say is the “target” in reforming society?
options: The laws of the country
Not quite. The article says: The thinking of the individual mind.
The wealth of the community
Not quite. The article says: The thinking of the individual mind.
The leaders in power
Not quite. The article says: The thinking of the individual mind.
The thinking of the individual mind
Yes. “As he thinketh in his heart, so is he.”
questions.rationale: “The correct starting point is to address the individual mind with the aim of revolutionizing the thinking of the individual. This is the right way of social reform.”

questions.q: On seeing Maxwell’s equations, the physicist Boltzmann exclaimed, “Who was the God who wrote these signs?” What does the article draw from such reactions?
options: The order and meaning found in nature point an open mind to a supreme intelligence
Right. A biased mind stays in the dark amid the light.
Nature can be known only through equations
Not quite. The article says: The order and meaning found in nature point an open mind to a supreme intelligence.
Scientists are usually religious people
Not quite. The article says: The order and meaning found in nature point an open mind to a supreme intelligence.
Mathematics is a form of worship
Not quite. The article says: The order and meaning found in nature point an open mind to a supreme intelligence.
questions.rationale: “Every study of the Universe shows that it has not been randomly put together but impeccably planned… Nature is a sign of God and speaks to us about God.”

questions.article: Learn the Art of Ego Management
questions.q: Does the article treat the ego as something bad in itself?
options: Yes – it is the mark of a weak person
Not quite. The article says: No – it is a source of confidence and resolve; trouble arises when it is provoked in dealings with others.
No – it should be given free rein
Not quite. The article says: No – it is a source of confidence and resolve; trouble arises when it is provoked in dealings with others.
No – it is a source of confidence and resolve; trouble arises when it is provoked in dealings with others
Yes. So it has to be managed, not destroyed.
Yes – it should be rooted out completely
Not quite. The article says: No – it is a source of confidence and resolve; trouble arises when it is provoked in dealings with others.
questions.rationale: “Ego is a healthy phenomenon… It is this negative aspect that creates problems” in social life, where differences lead to clashes.

questions.article: Learn the Art of Ego Management
questions.q: The article calls ego management “the price of social living.” What does it mean?
options: Society charges a fee for membership
Not quite. The article says: The benefits of living among others come only to one who accepts their “thorns” along with their “flowers”.
The benefits of living among others come only to one who accepts their “thorns” along with their “flowers”
Well read. Each person is like a rose plant.
Living alone is the cheaper choice
Not quite. The article says: The benefits of living among others come only to one who accepts their “thorns” along with their “flowers”.
One must pay others to keep the peace
Not quite. The article says: The benefits of living among others come only to one who accepts their “thorns” along with their “flowers”.
questions.rationale: “If one wants to enjoy the benefits of social living one will have to learn the art of ego management… One has to accept the thorn in the same way that one accepts the flower.”

questions.q: The article likens life before death and life after death to two things. Which?
options: A school and a playground
Not quite. The article says: A temporary nursery and a permanent garden.
A journey and its starting point
Not quite. The article says: A temporary nursery and a permanent garden.
A river and the sea
Not quite. The article says: A temporary nursery and a permanent garden.
A temporary nursery and a permanent garden
Correct. Now is the time of preparation; then, of reward.
questions.rationale: “The pre-death period of life is like a temporary nursery and the post-death period is like a permanent garden.”

questions.q: “Man’s life is like an iceberg.” What does the article mean by this?
options: Life is cold and hard
Not quite. The article says: Only a small tip lies in this world; the greater part lies in the Hereafter.
Only a small tip lies in this world; the greater part lies in the Hereafter
Yes. So one should prepare for what is to come.
Life is dangerous to those who come near
Not quite. The article says: Only a small tip lies in this world; the greater part lies in the Hereafter.
Life melts away quickly
Not quite. The article says: Only a small tip lies in this world; the greater part lies in the Hereafter.
questions.rationale: “Only a small tip of his life lies in the present world; the rest of it lies in the world Hereafter.”

questions.q: How does the article describe “much remembrance” of God (zikr-e-kathir)?
options: Reciting set words many times a day
Not quite. The article says: A chain of reflection in which each thought about God’s work leads to the next.
Remaining silent for long periods
Not quite. The article says: A chain of reflection in which each thought about God’s work leads to the next.
A chain of reflection in which each thought about God’s work leads to the next
Exactly. Rain, for example, sets a prepared mind thinking step by step.
Attending many religious gatherings
Not quite. The article says: A chain of reflection in which each thought about God’s work leads to the next.
questions.rationale: “Remembering God much, is a result of a chain reaction in the thinking process; that is, a series of thoughts in which each thought causes the next one.”

questions.q: Why, says the article, do many people who were successful in their careers feel lost after retirement?
options: They did not work hard enough
Not quite. The article says: For years they played a role and left their own personality undeveloped.
Their friends forget them
Not quite. The article says: For years they played a role and left their own personality undeveloped.
For years they played a role and left their own personality undeveloped
Right. Like an actor returning from the set.
They no longer have enough money
Not quite. The article says: For years they played a role and left their own personality undeveloped.
questions.rationale: “Having assumed the role of another personality in his professional life, he returns to his original self in his retired life. The original personality however has remained in an underdeveloped state.”

questions.q: A lost child stops crying the moment his mother picks him up. What is this a picture of, in the article?
options: A child’s need for discipline
Not quite. The article says: Man’s search, which comes to rest only when he finds God for himself.
The weakness of human beings
Not quite. The article says: Man’s search, which comes to rest only when he finds God for himself.
Man’s search, which comes to rest only when he finds God for himself
Yes. The test of having found Him is complete satisfaction.
The comfort that wealth brings
Not quite. The article says: Man’s search, which comes to rest only when he finds God for himself.
questions.rationale: “Everyone, knowingly or unknowingly, is in search of God… when you find Him, you should become completely satisfied, like the little boy.”

questions.q: Why does the article say simplicity can be called “a part of faith”?
options: Poverty is required of believers
Not quite. The article says: A simple life frees the mind from distraction, so that it can be given to higher things.
A simple life frees the mind from distraction, so that it can be given to higher things
Well reasoned. “High thinking is the result of simple living.”
Complex things are forbidden
Not quite. The article says: A simple life frees the mind from distraction, so that it can be given to higher things.
Simple people are easier to teach
Not quite. The article says: A simple life frees the mind from distraction, so that it can be given to higher things.
questions.rationale: “If we adopt simplicity in our lives, then we will save ourselves from many distractions. Only then will it be possible for us to use our faculties for higher thinking.”
